page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for balanced compute and memory workloads. The instance features an x86_64 processor architecture configured with 2 dedicated virtual CPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory. This yields a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM distribution, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per processor core for predictable execution without memory contention.

From an infrastructure and hardware perspective, the n4d-standard-2 includes dedicated CPU allocation, separating its compute performance from the noisy-neighbor variability of shared or burstable tiers. The instance provisions no hardware accelerators or local storage disks, operating entirely with detached network-based block storage. Networking configuration specifies zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires explicit external routing or NAT gateway provisioning for direct internet access.

In terms of qualitative efficiency and application sizing, the configuration matches standard general-purpose computing ratios. It provides consistent resource density for workloads that do not demand heavy I/O operations or accelerated GPU computing. Ideal workload profiles include lightweight web application serving, backend API microservices, staging environments, small-scale task runners, and modular background processing services.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-2 is a general-purpose compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Designed to deliver predictable performance, it provides 2 dedicated virtual CPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no bundled hardware accelerators or local storage disks, necessitating the use of attached network-based storage volumes for operating systems and persistent data. Additionally, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. With dedicated CPU allocation, the n4d-standard-2 avoids the resource contention common in burstable shared-core tiers, offering reliable single- and dual-threaded processing efficiency. The symmetrical memory-to-core balance makes this server practical for lightweight web serving, containerized microservices, small API gateways, continuous integration agents, and standard application development environments that require steady compute without extreme memory or storage throughput requirements.
